title: 3.1.3 Quiz: Identify the Function Calls
description: Spot which lines are function calls and count how many run. Checked instantly.

questions.question: Which line has a function call?
questions.explanation: Lines 1 and 2 are assignments: they store a value using arithmetic, they do not run a job. Line 3, console.log(offsetNum), is a name followed by parentheses — that is what a call looks like.

questions.question: How many times is console.log() called?
questions.explanation: console.log() runs on lines 1, 4, and 5 — three times. The two prompt() calls on lines 2 and 3 are function calls too, but the question only asks about console.log().

questions.question: How many function calls are there in total?
questions.explanation: Number(...) runs twice and prompt(...) runs twice — four calls — plus one console.log(...). Five sets of parentheses, five calls.

questions.question: Is Math.PI a function call?
options: Yes — it has a dot, so it must be a method
No — it is a stored value with no parentheses after it
Only on the first time it is used
questions.explanation: Parentheses mean "run it now." Math.PI is a name you read, not a job you order — no parentheses, no call. Math.sqrt(16) would be a call.

questions.question: Which statement calls a function named printPcSpecs?
questions.explanation: printPcSpecs on its own just names the function without running it. function printPcSpecs() starts a definition, not a call. Only printPcSpecs() — name plus parentheses — actually runs it.
